data.summary: Unchanged supplied color trace confirmed 5/5 with all eight checkpoint images. Explicit assistance and the earlier inconclusive selection remain recorded.
Tracing observed behavior into the pre-fix source.

data.root_cause: Most likely localization is the hexadecimal-input path in ColorPicker: after parsing the entered text into `current`, it immediately derives HSV and reconstructs `current` from HSV before OK submits it. That RGB→HSV→RGB round trip occurs before the Colored Floor/Wall caller packs the color to RGBA8888. It is therefore the shared source-level path capable of changing `ff0300` before either tile type stores or rereads it; the precise one-channel rounding behavior inside Arc's unavailable Color implementation is not directly inspectable here.
data.subsystem: Shared UI color picker used by map-editor configurable colored environment tiles

evidence: Lines 133-150 parse text with `Color.valueOf(current, value)`, convert that parsed RGB color with `current.toHsv(values)`, then call `updateColor(false)`.
Lines 175-177 show that `updateColor(false)` executes `current.fromHsv(h, s, v)` and restores alpha, so the parsed color is reconstructed before acceptance.

Lines 165-168 submit this reconstructed `current` through `cons.get(current)`. Because the false argument suppresses field rewriting at lines 179-185, the text field can retain the typed string while the committed Color object has gone through the conversion.
On a subsequent dialog opening, line 133 initializes the field from `current.toString()`, matching the replay's distinction between entry and later picker readback.
candidates.reasoning: The recorded replay reports the same ff0300-to-ff0200 readback for both Colored Wall and Colored Floor. This is the only inspected shared code path that parses typed hexadecimal input and mutates the Color object before either tile-specific callback receives it.

evidence: Lines 47-62 open `ui.picker.show(..., false, col -> block.lastConfig = col.rgba8888())`; thus the picker result is converted to the stored integer configuration at the boundary after ColorPicker's input handling.

ColoredWall.buildEditorConfig at core/src/mindustry/world/blocks/environment/ColoredWall.java:39-41 delegates to this exact shared method, explaining why both reported tile types use the same picker/packing path.

ColoredFloor lines 176-185 and ColoredWall lines 60-69 assign the Integer configuration to `tile.extraData` and retrieve it into `lastConfig` without another visible color-space conversion. MapEditor.drawBlocks at core/src/mindustry/editor/MapEditor.java:201-203 passes `drawBlock.lastConfig` to `placeEnded`.
The shared caller therefore is the immediate commit/readback bridge, but its code points upstream to ColorPicker for the mutation.
candidates.reasoning: This is the common integration point for Colored Floor and Colored Wall and packs the post-picker floating Color to the persisted integer. It is a secondary candidate because packing can expose a sub-8-bit difference introduced by the picker, while the inspected tile storage/pick methods themselves appear to preserve the integer.

limitations: This was a source-only review. I did not execute the game or inspect the listed image artifacts in this stage. The supplied replay is recorded evidence of 5 successful out of 5 deterministic runs at the supplied commit, not a run performed here.

The Arc dependency implementation of `Color.valueOf`, `Color.toHsv`, `Color.fromHsv`, and `Color.rgba8888` was not present in the inspectable repository search results. Consequently, source review establishes the lossy-looking round-trip location but cannot independently identify the exact floating-point, slider, or integer-packing operation responsible for the one-value decrement.

The supplied replay specifically establishes the ff0300 workflow for both tile types; this review did not independently validate every additional reported table entry, Windows/build comparisons, save/archive behavior, or screenshot contents.
No conclusion is offered about a future fix; the inspected code only localizes the currently recorded behavior.

data.summary: Saving the confirmed replay as an executable regression test.
Designing a small candidate diff in the disposable repository.

data.explanation: Remove the HSV-to-RGB reconstruction immediately after `Color.valueOf(current, value)` parses hex text. The parsed `current` color is already exact; the callback still updates the HSV state and slider positions for UI consistency. Consequently, pressing OK without changing a slider sends the parsed RGB value to the Colored Floor/Wall callback, which then packs and stores that value unchanged.
risks: This changes hex-entry behavior for every caller of the shared ColorPicker, not only colored environment tiles. That scope is intentional because the lossy conversion is in the shared picker path.

After direct hex entry, subsequent slider interaction still intentionally derives a color from HSV and may quantize according to slider precision; this patch only preserves exact text input when no slider edit is made.
Validation should exercise six- and eight-digit input, alpha-enabled and alpha-disabled picker callers, invalid/intermediate text, direct OK, reopen/readback, and slider edits after text entry.
